Maintenance Report — MNT-0023-005

Asset: WELL-0023 (SW-23 Well 023, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 26 Aug 2023 08:00 · Finished: 29 Aug 2023 14:00 · Well stopped for this job: 78 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0023-0045 on 2023-08-24 Report written: 30 Aug 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the wellhead was cold and the pump jack was straining with a heavy, uneven load. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0023-0045 showed the wellhead at 36.0 °C with the air at 33.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 1 day for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Sand and scale build-up in the pump barrel.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0023-007

Asset: WELL-0023 (SW-23 Well 023, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 15 Dec 2023 08:00 · Finished: 15 Dec 2023 21:00 · Well stopped for this job: 13 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Daniel Foster · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0023-0061 on 2023-12-14 Report written: 16 Dec 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0023-0061 at 15:15 on 2023-12-14 found crude oil on the pad: about 9.8% of the pad area, estimated 3.6 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 6.2 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a corrosion hole along the flowline route.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 8 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 3% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 269 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 215 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.4 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0023-007 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.3% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0023-010

Asset: WELL-0023 (SW-23 Well 023, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 01 Mar 2024 08:00 · Finished: 27 Mar 2024 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 634 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward, Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0023-0072 on 2024-02-29 Report written: 29 Mar 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator found an oil puddle under the gearbox. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0023-0072 showed the wellhead at 11.3 °C with the air at 11.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 24 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

A hardened output shaft seal after years of service.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).

  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0023-010 (WS-06).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0023-012

Asset: WELL-0023 (SW-23 Well 023, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 07 Apr 2024 08:00 · Finished: 23 Apr 2024 08:00 · Well stopped for this job: 384 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0023-0077 on 2024-04-04 Report written: 23 Apr 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the electric motor driving the pump jack had stopped and would not restart. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0023-0077 showed the wellhead at 21.6 °C with the air at 16.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 14 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Winding breakdown from heat and age.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0023-030

Asset: WELL-0023 (SW-23 Well 023, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 04 Sep 2026 08:00 · Finished: 22 Sep 2026 11:00 · Well stopped for this job: 435 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0023-0201 on 2026-09-03 Report written: 23 Sep 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0023-0201 showed the wellhead at 31.0 °C with the air at 29.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 16 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.
